summary: Based on evidence through November 13 2018, the only substantive change justified is to loosen the First Lien Net Leverage Ratio floor in C01 due to strong EBITDA performance; all other covenants remain appropriate as-is.

clauses.rationale: Evidence shows 2018 EBITDA guidance of $40‑45 million and rising net sales, indicating the leverage ratio may fall below the current floor, risking breach; thus the floor should be loosened.
clauses.change: Lower the minimum First Lien Net Leverage Ratio floor (make the covenant less restrictive)

evidence.quote: Adjusted EBITDA of $40 million to $45 million, an increase of 79% to 102% year-over-year*
Consolidated net sales of approximately $515 million, an increase of approximately 93% year-over-year

clauses.rationale: No new evidence indicates a change is needed to the annual financial statement and compliance certificate delivery requirement.
Quarterly reporting obligations remain supported by the available evidence; no amendment is warranted.
Monthly reporting obligations remain appropriate; no evidence justifies a change.
Evidence of strong performance and raised guidance shows no material adverse effect, so the notice provisions remain adequate.
The amended revolving credit facility increase to $75 million stays within the permitted basket; no evidence suggests a need to adjust indebtedness restrictions.

drift_reasons: Evidence of robust EBITDA and net sales growth indicates the First Lien Net Leverage Ratio floor may be too high, justifying a loosening of that threshold, which alters permitted behavior and risk coverage.
